payload.title: Mauritius Wedding Legal Requirements and Steps
payload.excerpt: Mauritius is on the shortlist, and before you fall for a lagoon you want to know one thing: will the marriage count? In most cases, yes.
key_takeaways: Two Australians marry legally in Mauritius through the Civil Status Division's civil process for two non-citizens, celebrated by a Civil Status Officer.
Your application must reach the Central Civil Status Office in Port Louis at least one month before the wedding, with documents forwarded 6 to 8 weeks ahead.
Once you land, you visit the Office together with your original documents before the 24-hour publication and the ceremony.
Keep your original marriage certificate safe, because only originals (or copies certified by a notary and the Supreme Court) can take an Apostille.

faq.q: Is a civil marriage in Mauritius recognised in Australia?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. An overseas marriage is generally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law. You cannot register it in Australia, and your Mauritian certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage.

faq.q: How early do we need to arrive in Mauritius before the wedding?
faq.a: Early enough to visit the Central Civil Status Office in Port Louis with your original documents, receive your Certificate of Authority and allow the 24-hour publication before the ceremony. Ask the Office how many working days to allow, and add a spare day for flights.

faq.q: Do we need witnesses for a civil wedding in Mauritius?
faq.a: Yes. Two witnesses must be present at the ceremony. Choose them before you travel and ask the Office what identification they should bring.

faq.q: Can we marry on the beach in Mauritius?
faq.a: The civil marriage can be celebrated at hotels and any private or non-private premises, not only at the Office. Ask your resort whether the beach in front of it can host the civil ceremony, whether any permission is needed, and who arranges the Officer's transport.

Birth certificates must be drawn up in English or French. Australian birth certificates are in English. For any other document, such as a divorce or name change record issued in another language, ask the Office what it needs.

faq.q: Can we have a religious or symbolic ceremony as well?
faq.a: The civil ceremony before a Civil Status Officer is the legal route for two non-citizens. You can add a symbolic ceremony on the same day. For a religious ceremony, ask the Office and your celebrant how it would sit alongside the civil marriage.
